extracted.intended_audience: researchers and authors preparing evidence synthesis protocols (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, scoping reviews) and librarians who support them
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on where and how to pre-register protocols for evidence syntheses (systematic reviews, meta-analyses, scoping reviews), with discipline-matching registry recommendations and registry-specific notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Register a Protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Register your evidence synthesis protocol (step in the evidence synthesis workflow).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This page lists registries to consider for pre-registering systematic review and other evidence synthesis protocols; registration documents key protocol elements and provides a time-stamped public record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose a registry appropriate to your discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a registry that matches your subject area and review type (the page provides discipline-specific registry suggestions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide is not comprehensive; choose between multidisciplinary registries (e.g., OSF) and discipline-specific registries (e.g., Cochrane for healthcare, Campbell for social policy, CEE for environmental issues, PROSPERO for health and social care). Email the library service to learn more about registry options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open Science Framework (OSF) — multidisciplinary pre-registration
rubrics_metrics.description: OSF is an open source, multidisciplinary web application used to pre-register systematic review protocols and share project materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Researchers can use OSF to collaborate, document, archive, share, and register projects; share materials such as a Zotero library, search strategies, and data extraction forms. Evidence synthesis author teams do not submit their protocols for review by an editorial board before they are accepted and pre-registered on OSF; instead, create your own pre-registration. OSF provides a Generalized Systematic Review Registration Form designed for use across disciplines and evidence synthesis types (e.g., scoping reviews, meta-analysis). Example pre-registered protocols are available for reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cochrane — health-focused benchmark registry/organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Cochrane produces high-quality, relevant, accessible systematic reviews and other synthesized research evidence, widely recognized as a benchmark for effectiveness of health care.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider Cochrane for evidence syntheses in healthcare where the highest methodological standards and international recognition are important; Cochrane operates as an editorial and production organization for systematic reviews rather than a simple registry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campbell Collaboration — social policy and related disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: Campbell promotes production and use of systematic reviews for evidence-based policy and practice in areas such as business, education, crime and justice, international development, nutrition, social welfare, and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Campbell when your review topic falls within its subject domains and when aiming to inform policy and practice; Campbell provides standards and infrastructure for reviews in these fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration for Environmental Evidence (CEE) — environmental syntheses
rubrics_metrics.description: CEE is an open community that promotes and delivers evidence syntheses focused on environmental policy, biodiversity conservation, and related sustainability issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CEE for environment-focused reviews; CEE provides community-driven standards and venues for environmental evidence syntheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: PROSPERO — international database for prospectively registered systematic reviews (health & related fields)
rubrics_metrics.description: PROSPERO is an international database of prospectively registered systematic reviews in health and social care (and related areas). Key features from the review protocol are recorded and maintained as a permanent record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROSPERO is appropriate for many health- and social care-related systematic reviews but does not accept scoping reviews. Use PROSPERO when you need a prospectively-registered, maintained public record of key protocol elements.
